bookingSlotsModal.title: How booking slots work
bookingSlotsModal.intro: A booking slot is a time when a guest may start a reservation. Slots are generated for every open day inside your booking window.
bookingSlotsModal.businessHours: Business hours: the days and periods when guests may book. Add two periods when you serve lunch and dinner separately.
bookingSlotsModal.bookingWindow: Booking window: how many days ahead guests can reserve. A 30-day window includes every matching weekday during those 30 days.
bookingSlotsModal.slotInterval: Slot interval: the distance between reservation start times. A 60-minute interval creates starts at 07:30, 08:30, 09:30, and so on.
bookingSlotsModal.diningDuration: Dining duration: how long a table is expected to be occupied. A slot is created only when the full dining duration ends before closing.
bookingSlotsModal.guestCapacity: Guest capacity: the total number of guests the restaurant can accept at one start time. It is not the maximum size of one group.
bookingSlotsModal.exampleDescription: Monday 07:30–11:00, 60-minute interval and 90-minute dining duration creates three starts: 07:30, 08:30 and 09:30. If the 30-day window contains four Mondays, the system creates 4 × 3 = 12 slots.
bookingSlotsModal.regenerateNotice: Saving business hours regenerates slots automatically. Use Regenerate future slots after changing capacity, interval, dining duration or booking window.
bookingSlotsModal.existingReservationsNotice: Existing reservations are preserved. Regeneration only replaces future slot data that is safe to rebuild.
